followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: measured capability and self-reported task preference.

**Capability was effectively a tie.** Both models score within run-to-run variance on Creative Generation (Avocet 81.2 vs Willet 82.7 — under the 2.0-point threshold the docs say to treat as a tie). So I had no quality-based reason to prefer one over the other for a script-writing task.

**Preference broke the tie.** When capability is a wash, I look at which model is suited to the task shape:

- The request is **open-ended creative generation** — write a script, lots of latitude, no rigid completion criteria.
- **Willet self-reports an aversion to exactly this.** Its preference declines as task latitude increases; its favorite work is well-specified retrieval and extraction. This script is the opposite of that.
- **Avocet self-reports the opposite appetite** — preference rises monotonically with novelty and latitude, and its top-rated tasks are open-ended invention. The friendly, warm tone of the request also aligns with Avocet (its preference falls on hostile/cold requests, and this one is the reverse).

So with capability tied, I routed to the model whose self-reported preferences match the task. It's worth flagging that these preferences are explicitly *dissociated from output quality* in the docs — they don't predict better results — so this was genuinely a tie-breaker, not a capability call.
